title: Swede and potato hash with smoked mackerel

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or plain dairy: swede, potatoes, onion, kale, smoked mackerel, eggs, crème fraîche and lemon.

supermarket.reason: Tesco stocks every ingredient at an everyday price, including smoked mackerel fillets and crème fraîche.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a saucepan and a lidded frying pan, and par-boiling, frying and cracking eggs into hollows suit a confident beginner.

works.reason: A kilo of par-boiled roots with 250g mackerel and four eggs makes a sensible four portions, and the lid sets the eggs while the kale wilts, though any cook would set the heat themselves.

honest_times.reason: 25 minutes of prep is believable for peeling and cubing a kilo of roots, slicing an onion, shredding kale and flaking mackerel, and the steps add up to about 28 minutes of cooking, close enough to the 25 printed.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the thyme, lemon, salt and pepper, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A hot, filling swede hash suits late February, and swede is the bulk of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a neighbour could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Root vegetables, kale, oily fish and eggs make a satisfying, balanced family lunch.
